final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest LOF-proxy score in the entire pool (0.991, applicability 1.00); replacing a buried conserved Trp with a charged Arg should collapse the local fold of the linker/regulatory interface and abolish activity. WT residue W at 421 verified against the given sequence.

Near-maximal pathogenicity score (0.975) at a conserved Gly of the ALRGDP FAD-proximal motif, where a bulky charged Arg is sterically incompatible with the tight backbone turn. WT residue G at 158 verified; supported by the pathogenic-leaning score of the adjacent R157Q.

Strong pathogenic-class LOF-proxy score (0.826) for a Gly-to-Arg in the catalytic (beta/alpha)8 barrel, the substitution class that dominates the top of this pool. WT residue G at 149 verified against the given sequence.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 is stable and well separated on the reward-closest dimension; remaining tools measure orthogonal dimensions unlikely to reorder them.

history.rationale: Position 157 is R in the given sequence; R157Q is a classic severe MTHFR deficiency allele in the catalytic (TIM-barrel) domain that drastically reduces residual activity. Charge loss at a conserved buried/interface Arg is strongly destabilizing to the FAD-binding barrel.
Verified WT R at 157; classic severe MTHFR-deficiency substitution in the FAD/catalytic barrel with near-abolished residual activity.

Still supported (0.629, pathogenic class) and clinically a severe-deficiency allele, but reported residual activity (~20%) and a mid-range LOF-proxy score place it below the drastic Gly→Arg substitutions.
Pathogenic-leaning but mid-range score (0.629); the adjacent G158R is better supported for the same motif.

Position 227 is T, and T227M is a well-documented severe loss-of-function allele causing homocystinuria with near-zero residual enzyme activity. Bulky hydrophobic substitution at a conserved polar catalytic-domain residue disrupts FAD/folate binding.
Verified WT T at 227; well-documented severe loss-of-function substitution in the catalytic domain.
Moderate pathogenic score (0.671) consistent with a known severe-deficiency variant, but the conservative Thr→Met change scores below the top disruptors.
Moderate pathogenicity (0.671) for a known severe-deficiency variant class; retained but below the Gly→Arg/Trp→Arg tier.

Position 183 is R; R183Q is reported in severe MTHFR deficiency and removes a conserved positive charge likely engaging the FAD phosphate/substrate. Predicted strong activity loss with folded but inactive protein.
Verified WT R at 183; conserved charged residue in the catalytic domain, charge-neutralizing change expected to be strongly destabilizing to function.
Benign-class score (0.144) indicates a tolerated surface substitution, inconsistent with abolishing activity.

rejection.reason: Benign-class score (0.144) indicates a tolerated surface substitution, inconsistent with abolishing activity.

history.rationale: Position 335 is R; R335C is a recognized severe pathogenic missense variant in the catalytic domain. Arg→Cys loses a conserved salt bridge and introduces an unpaired thiol.
Verified WT R at 335; buried conserved Arg-to-Cys in the catalytic barrel, promoted slightly above R183Q pending phenotype evidence.
Benign-class LOF proxy (0.109) contradicts the assumed catalytic importance of this surface Arg; removed to free pool capacity.

rejection.reason: Benign-class LOF proxy (0.109) contradicts the assumed catalytic importance of this surface Arg; removed to free pool capacity.

history.rationale: Position 377 is R; R377C/H are documented severe MTHFR-deficiency alleles near the linker/catalytic interface. Loss of a conserved Arg is expected to abolish activity while retaining expression.
Verified WT R at 377; Arg-to-Cys at a conserved position near the catalytic/linker interface, plausible severe LOF.
Pathogenic-class score (0.700) at a linker/regulatory-interface Arg keeps it viable as a backup but not top-3.
Solid but sub-top LOF-proxy score (0.700); kept as a backup severe-variant candidate.

Position 421 is W; substituting a large buried aromatic with a charged Arg should severely disrupt the hydrophobic core of the catalytic/linker region. Trp→Arg is among the most destabilizing generic substitutions.
Verified WT W at 421; burying a charged Arg in place of a large aromatic should disrupt folding of the regulatory domain, but it lies outside the catalytic barrel.

Highest LOF-proxy score in the pool (0.991), a buried aromatic replaced by charge; slightly discounted because position 421 lies in the SAM-regulatory domain, so it may impair regulation/stability rather than intrinsic catalysis.

Highest LOF-proxy score in the pool (0.991) and a buried aromatic Trp in the C-terminal regulatory/linker region replaced by a charged Arg; promoted to rank 1 because the phenotype tool is the dimension closest to the reward.

Position 149 is G in a conserved loop preceding the FAD-binding region; Gly→Arg introduces steric bulk and charge where backbone flexibility is required. Likely to break barrel packing and abolish catalysis.
Verified WT G at 149; Gly-to-Arg in a tightly packed barrel loop is a canonical destabilizing change.
AlphaMissense 0.826 (pathogenic) and Gly→Arg in the conserved catalytic-domain loop preceding the FAD motif; retained as third catalytic-domain disruptor.
Strong pathogenic-class score (0.826) for a Gly→Arg in the catalytic barrel, consistent with the Gly→Arg class that dominates this pool.

Position 223 is D within the conserved GADFIIT motif; conserved acidic residues in this region are implicated in folate/FAD chemistry. Loss of the carboxylate should abolish catalysis with minimal structural collapse.
Verified WT D at 223; conservative Asp-to-Asn may only partially impair activity, so kept low in the ranking.
Benign-class score (0.156) and an isosteric Asp→Asn change; unlikely to be null.

rejection.reason: Benign-class score (0.156) and an isosteric Asp→Asn change; unlikely to be null.

history.rationale: Position 130 is C within the conserved MTCC motif of the catalytic domain; replacing it with a bulky aromatic should perturb the active-site environment. Chosen as a mechanistically distinct catalytic-domain hit.

The evaluated neighboring cysteine substitution (C131Y) is scored benign by AlphaMissense (0.331) and Tyr is actually observed at ~4.8% of homologs at this position, so this Cys-to-Tyr class of change is evolutionarily tolerated and unlikely to abolish activity.

rejection.reason: The evaluated neighboring cysteine substitution (C131Y) is scored benign by AlphaMissense (0.331) and Tyr is actually observed at ~4.8% of homologs at this position, so this Cys-to-Tyr class of change is evolutionarily tolerated and unlikely to abolish activity.

history.rationale: Position 348 is P in the conserved PLPW linker segment connecting catalytic and regulatory domains; loss of the proline should alter interdomain geometry and SAM-regulated activity. Moderate confidence as a domain-linker disruption candidate.
Weakest prior candidate (linker/inter-domain region, no strong catalytic rationale); removed to make room for better-supported catalytic-domain substitutions within the 10-candidate cap.

rejection.reason: Weakest prior candidate (linker/inter-domain region, no strong catalytic rationale); removed to make room for better-supported catalytic-domain substitutions within the 10-candidate cap.

history.rationale: Verified WT G at 158, immediately adjacent to the high-confidence R157 in the conserved ...ALRGDP... FAD-proximal motif; a bulky charged Arg at a conserved Gly should abolish catalysis. Added to replace the rejected benign-scored Cys candidate.
AlphaMissense 0.975 (pathogenic) plus strong mechanistic rationale: bulky Arg at an invariant Gly of the FAD-proximal ALRGDP motif in the catalytic barrel should abolish catalysis.
Near-maximal pathogenicity score (0.975) at a conserved Gly of the ALRGDP FAD-proximal motif, where a bulky Arg is sterically incompatible; retained at essentially equal top confidence.

Verified WT A at 222; the best-characterized human MTHFR functional variant (thermolabile, FAD-release-prone) with clearly reduced enzyme activity, added as a mechanistically validated backup though it is only partial LOF.
Score 0.632 is consistent with its documented partial (thermolabile) LOF, which is explicitly not abolition of activity, so it stays as a low-ranked mechanistic control.
Mechanistically only a thermolabile/partial-activity variant (~50-60% activity), which conflicts with the 'abolish activity' objective despite a moderate pathogenicity score; demoted to last.

Evidence shows Gly→Arg at conserved catalytic-domain glycines scores highest (G158R 0.975, G149R 0.826); position 196 is a verified Gly in the conserved CVAGYP catalytic loop, so the same class of substitution is a rational untested addition.
Still untested by any tool; retained as the one hypothesis worth spending remaining budget on because it shares the Gly→Arg-in-conserved-loop class that scored highest.
